country.comment: Study examines informal settlements in the Conurbano Bonaerense within the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Area (Región Metropolitana de Buenos Aires, RMBA), Argentina.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumen & Ideas destacadas; PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF p. 3, Introducción; PDF p. 4, Figura 1

effect_estimate.comment: Primary empirical analysis is qualitative (ethnography and semi-structured interviews); numeric coverage and program figures reported in the text are cited secondary descriptive statistics from AySA and TECHO.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Across two public utilities (OSN, 1983–1993; AySA, 2006–2015) and one private concessionaire (AASA, 1993–2006), residents of informal settlements in the Conurbano Bonaerense were excluded from turnkey utility network extension and accessed piped drinking water only through targeted alternative schemes (Pro-agua, informal political brokerage, Mecanismo Participativo de Gestión, and Agua + Trabajo [A+T]) requiring direct resident labor and local intermediaries (Peronist party brokers/'punteros' and later piquetero-linked worker cooperatives) backed by insufficient state materials, training, and technical supervision. Cited secondary data show that by 2015–2016 piped water coverage reached ~78% in the RMBA overall versus 12% via formal connections in informal settlements, and by end-2015 only 99 A+T modules were completed (408 km of network serving an estimated 165,294 people, compared with 484 unfinished modules and >3,300,000 inhabitants incorporated in formal neighborhoods), while co-produced networks in the Santa María case suffered delays, frequent breaks, service cuts, low pressure, and contamination.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumen; PDF p. 4–5, Introducción; PDF p. 10, Prácticas y políticas focalizadas; PDF p. 12 & 15, Desde el barrio & Conclusiones

mechanism_certainty.comment: Qualitative ethnographic case study appraised with CASP (design ceiling = 2). Through 2011–2015 fieldwork in Santa María, semi-structured interviews with utility/regulatory officials and local intermediaries, and cooperative plans/sketches (Figure 3), the authors directly observe and trace how targeted co-production schemes, delegation of construction to under-trained cooperatives, outdated municipal cadastral maps of unlegalized land, and political brokerage delay network extension and compromise water service quality and continuity.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 5, Introducción; PDF p. 6–10, Prácticas y políticas focalizadas; PDF p. 11–15, Desde el barrio I & II; Figura 2 (PDF p. 10) & Figura 3 (PDF p. 14)

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines informal land tenure and unlegalized settlement status affecting billing and municipal cadastres (tenure, planning); targeted co-produced programs (Pro-agua, MPG, A+T) substituting resident/cooperative labor for turnkey utility provision (accommodation, participation, procedural_steps, delay); discretionary selection of neighborhoods and cooperatives by mayors and political brokers (discretion, political_coordination); friction across national utilities/regulators, provincial ministries, and municipalities (institutional_fragmentation); and insufficient state training, tools, and technical supervision (bureaucratic_assistance).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, tenure, planning, procedural_steps, delay, discretion, accommodation, participation, political_coordination, institutional_fragmentation, bureaucratic_assistance
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 3 & 5, Introducción; PDF p. 6–10, Prácticas y políticas focalizadas; PDF p. 11–15, Desde el barrio I & II; Figura 2 (PDF p. 10)

outcome_flags.comment: Focuses on piped drinking water access, formal vs. alternative connections, regional/program service coverage, implementation delays/unfinished modules, and observed pipe breaks, service interruptions/cuts, low pressure, and contamination in Santa María. Footnote 1 (PDF p. 3) explicitly notes sanitation is excluded for space reasons.
outcome_flags.value: water_access, formal_connection, service_coverage, service_continuity, service_reliability, service_quality, delay
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 3–5, Introducción (including Footnote 1); PDF p. 10, Prácticas y políticas focalizadas; PDF p. 12–15, Desde el barrio I & II

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary empirical study is a qualitative ethnographic case study (2011–2015 ethnography in Santa María, semi-structured interviews with officials and key informants, and public document analysis); descriptive statistics mentioned are secondary context figures from AySA, INDEC, and TECHO rather than a primary quantitative component, so CASP Qualitative Checklist applies rather than MMAT.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 5, Introducción; PDF p. 6–15, empirical sections

sample_size.comment: The paper specifies ethnographic fieldwork in 1 informal settlement (pseudonym 'Santa María', Conurbano Bonaerense, 2011–2015) reconstructing 2 intermediary water-extension episodes (puntero Báez and A+T cooperative worker Espina), supplemented by semi-structured interviews with public officials, regulatory staff, and local informants (at least 14 distinct interviewees cited across excerpts) and public documents, but does not report the exact total number of interviews or documents analyzed.
sample_size.value: 1 informal settlement ('Santa María', Conurbano Bonaerense, ethnographic fieldwork 2011–2015, 2 embedded cases); total number of semi-structured interviews and documents not reported
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 5–6, Introducción; PDF p. 6–15, interview and fieldwork citations

study_design.comment: Qualitative research design combining multi-year ethnographic fieldwork in a single informal settlement with semi-structured interviews, public document review, and secondary descriptive statistics across historical utility periods (1983–2015).
study_design.value: Qualitative case study and ethnography (ethnographic fieldwork 2011–2015 in an informal settlement combined with semi-structured interviews with public officials and key informants, public document analysis, and secondary descriptive statistics covering 1983–2015)
